title: The Ghost of Kowloon
premise: Dominic Whitlock, a financial-crimes investigator who has spent years laundering his own past into a spotless new identity, is living in a witness-protection safe house when a real-estate listing appears online featuring photos of the interior — including his go-bag by the door. The leak traces to a Hong Kong syndicate he once helped dismantle, whose surviving lieutenant, Vivian Chao, wants the ledger of offshore accounts Dominic memorized before it burned. Hunted through Kowloon's walled tenements by both the syndicate and a corrupt handler inside his own agency, Dominic allies with a street-level network of undocumented workers and a disgraced journalist, discovering the found family he never let himself have. In the climax he trades the ledger — the secret worth killing for — by broadcasting it publicly, destroying its value and exposing his handler, but at the cost of his protected identity; he ends the book nameless but finally free, choosing to stay in Kowloon with the people who saved him.
about_author: Dominic Pemberton is a former compliance officer who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers from a small flat in Lisbon, drawing on real-world financial forensics and the quiet loneliness of people who live under other names.

chapters.title: The Clean Room
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In a grey Manchester safe house, Dominic rehearses his cover identity over morning coffee, cataloguing the lies that keep him alive. The emotional beat is suffocating routine — a man so practiced at being no one he's forgotten who he was.

chapters.title: Listed
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A colleague sends him a property listing as a joke; the photos show his own kitchen, his go-bag by the door, the taped crack over the stove. Panic sets in as he realizes someone inside the program sold him. Beat: dread cracking through denial.

chapters.title: Go-Bag Protocol
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, intercut with the handler Marsh's. Dominic executes escape protocol but finds his extraction contact dead at the rendezvous. Marsh, meanwhile, logs a false location report. Beat: the machinery of protection revealed as the machinery of the hunt.

chapters.title: Vivian
chapters.summary: Vivian Chao's POV. In a Kowloon teahouse, Vivian — the syndicate's surviving accountant — reviews the listing photos and recognizes the ledger notebook in Dominic's bag. She orders him taken alive. Beat: cold competence masking a private debt she owes the dead.

chapters.title: The Long Layover
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Using cash and forged documents from a dead friend's emergency stash, Dominic flies to Hong Kong — the one place he's told never to go — because the listing agent's trail starts there. Beat: reckless agency; he stops running and starts hunting.

chapters.title: Chungking Mansions
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In the Mansions' labyrinth he traces the photographer, a teenage runner named Kit, and is nearly taken by syndicate muscle before Kit's aunt Mei hides him in a curry-house basement. Beat: first contact with the found family he'll come to need.

chapters.title: People Who Don't Exist
chapters.summary: Mei's POV. Mei, who shelters undocumented workers, sees through Dominic's fake name instantly and doesn't care. She offers a floor to sleep on in exchange for fixing a debt problem the syndicate is using to squeeze her tenants. Beat: guarded warmth.

chapters.title: The Ledger in His Head
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with flashbacks. We learn the ledger of offshore accounts exists only in Dominic's memory — he memorized and burned it before testifying. Vivian's people want it; so, it emerges, does someone inside his own agency. Beat: the secret's true weight revealed.

chapters.title: Handler
chapters.summary: Marsh's POV. Marsh meets Vivian's lieutenant and negotiates: the ledger for a clean exit and a cut. We see Marsh's corruption as banal — mortgage, mistress, resentment. Beat: banality of betrayal; the protector is the predator.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Kit is grabbed by the syndicate as leverage; a photo arrives with a deadline. Dominic must trade the ledger for the boy, knowing the trade ends in his death. Beat: the price of survival made flesh — someone else's survival, bought with his.

chapters.title: What Mei Knows
chapters.summary: Mei's POV. Mei reveals the syndicate's grip on the tenement is built on the same offshore accounts in Dominic's head — her neighbors' rents flow through them. His secret isn't abstract here; it's the architecture of their exploitation. Beat: moral reckoning.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He seeks out Ada Fong, a disgraced investigative journalist who once chased the same ledger and lost everything. She agrees to help — not to redeem herself, she says, but because the story was always hers too. Beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: Ghost Money
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada and Dominic map the account structure from his memory, finding a dormant account that still receives payments — meaning the syndicate's leadership is alive and someone senior is still feeding it. Beat: revelation that widens the conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Exchange, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The trade for Kit goes wrong when Marsh's men arrive to take both ledger and Dominic. In the chaos, Kit escapes but Mei is shot covering him. Beat: action climax of the middle act; the cost of trust made literal.

chapters.title: Hospital Lights
chapters.summary: Kit's POV. Kit keeps vigil over Mei and, for the first time, tells Dominic the truth: he took the listing photos for money, not knowing what they'd unleash. Dominic forgives him. Beat: guilt, forgiveness, the family hardening into something real.

chapters.title: Marsh's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada traces the dormant account's recent access to Marsh himself — he's been siphoning from the syndicate for years, and Vivian knows. Beat: the corruptor corrupted; leverage shifts to those with nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: The Devil's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. Vivian confronts Marsh, then offers Dominic a private deal: the ledger for Mei's hospital bills, Kit's safety, and his own life. He almost takes it. Beat: temptation — the elegant, corrupt solution that would cost him his soul.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Instead of trading the ledger, Dominic and Ada publish it in full — every account, every name, Marsh's included — destroying its value as a commodity and detonating the syndicate's finances. Beat: climax; the secret worth killing for, made worthless by giving it away.

chapters.title: Kowloon Nights
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The fallout cascades: Marsh is arrested, syndicate accounts frozen, Vivian vanishes mid-collapse — leaving Dominic a single note: 'You were the only honest one.' Beat: catharsis and vertigo as the old world burns.

chapters.title: No Name Given
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. His protection identity is burned; the agency disavows him to contain the scandal. Officially, Dominic Whitlock no longer exists anywhere. Standing in the tenement stairwell, he feels the strange lightness of being no one — and no one's target. Beat: loss transfigured into freedom.

chapters.title: The Sixth Floor
chapters.summary: Mei's POV. Mei, out of hospital, offers Dominic the empty sixth-floor room permanently. Kit teaches him the neighborhood; Ada files her comeback story. Beat: quiet belonging — the found family assembling itself around a man with nothing to offer but himself.

chapters.title: The Ghost of Kowloon
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Months later, a new listing appears online — photos of the sixth-floor room, taken from outside the window. Dominic smiles, unpacks the go-bag for good, and puts the kettle on. Beat: resolution with a held breath; survival, finally, as a place to stay.
